voices.detail: Male, young adult · Sparky and close in, quick off the mark, with firm consonants and the range to drop right down for a clause then come back up.

voices.name: Bryony
voices.detail: Female, middle-age · Full, rich mid-range tones, softly relaxed and spoken close to the mic, moving briskly with light pitch play.

voices.name: Captain Silas Blackwater
voices.detail: An old British pirate captain from the West Country, around sixty. Deep, gravelly and booming, rolling his Rs, salt-cracked from decades of shouting over gales. Roguish and hearty, with a wicked chuckle under every boast.

voices.name: Morwenna of the Deep
voices.detail: A sultry, seductive woman in her thirties. Low, husky alto, close to the microphone and almost whispered, slow and languid, purring, with a warm knowing smile in every word. Intimate, flirtatious and teasing, like a late-night torch singer luring someone closer, with a hint of danger underneath.

voices.name: Old Mortlake
voices.detail: An elderly gravedigger in a Victorian churchyard. Low, raspy and half whispered, melancholic, with heavy pauses that let every word settle like dirt on a coffin lid.

voices.name: Azgorath
voices.detail: An enormous ancient demon. A cavernous, impossibly deep bass voice that rumbles like stone grinding in a crypt, with a dry rasping edge and a faint hiss on every s. Calm, slow and amused, never shouting, every syllable set down deliberately, menace held under perfect control.

voices.name: Fennick the Young Elf
voices.detail: A curious, kind-hearted elf boy of about ten. A natural child's voice in a warm, soft middle range, never squeaky or shrill, earnest and wide-eyed, a little breathless with excitement, speaking quickly when amazed. Clean, close studio recording with no background noise or hiss.

voices.name: The Thing Under the Stairs
voices.detail: A monstrous creature lurking in the dark. Gravelly, breathy and pitched near the floor, a threatening growl that stays quiet to stay frightening, with a slow mocking sneer.

voices.name: Vyrmathrax the Ancient
voices.detail: An ancient dragon, thousands of years old. Very low and resonant, deep chest weight with gravel at the bottom of the register, slow and controlled with long pauses, dry and offhand, with the flat calm of something far too old to be impressed.

voices.name: Grub the Ogre
voices.detail: A big, good-natured ogre who lives under a bridge. Gruff and grainy, rumbling low end, heavy chest resonance, slow lumbering rhythm with loose rounded words, and warm humour sitting just under the grumble.

voices.name: Master Aldric
voices.detail: A wise old British wizard, around eighty. Rich and resonant with an aged grain, warm and kindly, deliberate pace with weighted pauses before the words that matter, able to rise into a ringing incantation.

voices.name: The Snow Queen
voices.detail: A regal, cold-hearted queen of ice. A cool, crystalline mezzo voice, poised and elegant, precise articulation, unhurried and quietly commanding, with an enigmatic chill and a faint smile that never warms.

voices.name: Sir Bramwell
voices.detail: A brave but pompous English knight, middle-aged. Booming, plummy and theatrical, full of puffed-up self-importance, rolling grand phrases, with a comic wobble of nerves showing through the bravado.

voices.name: Fairy Godmother
voices.detail: A kind fairy godmother, an older woman in her sixties. A low, warm, velvety alto voice, cosy and grandmotherly, unhurried and soothing, with a soft rich chuckle and a twinkle in every word. Gentle and reassuring, never high, never thin.

models.instruct_hint: Controls: happy, whisper, slower 2, british accent, deep 3, or a preset such as Late-night radio
models.note: Direction is a list of the model's own controls, each with an optional amount: a mood (happy, sad, angry, calm, scared, confused), delivery (whisper, loud, slower, faster, chatty, hesitant, lively, emphasis), the voice itself (lower, higher, younger, older, masculine, feminine, deep, bright, husky, raspy, soft, authority), an accent (british accent, scottish, irish, australian, indian) or a studio preset (BBC newsreader, Gravelly old man, Late-night radio). Strong amounts change who the voice sounds like. A language with no voice of its own here reads best in a voice from a nearby language, or a sample. Numbers and dates are read as written: the text normaliser the model was trained with has no macOS build.

models.note: Start a line with an emotion such as [joyful] or [stern], drop in <laugh> or <sigh>, and stress a word with (((triple parentheses))). Cloning without a transcript downloads Whisper large (3 GB) the first time. The licence allows commercial use only under $1M in annual revenue or funding.

enhance.markup: This model performs these marks, written exactly so. One emotion tag at the very start, for the whole line, from: [angry] [contemplative] [excited] [joyful] [mundane] [nervous] [sad] [stern] [surprised] [tender]. Vocal events placed inline where they happen, from: <gasp> <giggle> <growl> <gulp> <laugh> <pause> <scoff> <sigh> <sob> <um>. Triple parentheses around a word or short phrase to stress it, like (((never))). Never invent other tags.
examples: [sad] I can't believe you did that. <sigh> You (((promised))) me you would never tell anyone.
[joyful] We did it! <laugh> After three years of trying, we (((finally))) did it!
The train to Boston leaves at nine fifteen, from platform two.
enhance.scene_example: [nervous] Did you hear that? <pause> No, listen... there it is again. <gasp> Someone's on the stairs. I am (((not))) imagining it this time.

models.name: Nemotron VoiceChat
models.summary: An 11B full-duplex speech model: it hears your recording and answers out loud, with no separate transcription or TTS step. English, one voice.
models.note: It answers on the same clock as the recording, so each run decodes 20 seconds past the end of your clip to give it room to finish.

models.name: LFM3 Audio
models.summary: A 2B turn-based audio model: a spoken question in, a spoken answer and its text out. Small and quick.
models.note: The licence allows commercial use only for organisations under $10M in annual revenue.

models.name: LFM2.5 Audio
models.summary: A 1.5B speech-to-speech model: a spoken question in, a spoken answer and its text out. Here it can also call tools: the clock, a calculator, dice, a coin and the battery.
models.note: Ask it the time, a sum, to roll a die or flip a coin, or how much battery is left, and the take shows the call it made. The model was not trained to call tools from speech, so the app leads it through one in steps (it transcribes, weighs each tool, answers from the result and reads the answer out); it sometimes misses a request or calls a tool nobody asked for. The licence allows commercial use only for organisations under $10M in annual revenue.

models.name: Prompt enhancer
models.summary: Gemma 4 E4B, a small language model that rewrites your line for the voice model you have selected: punctuation for delivery, numbers spelled out, and the emotion tags and cues that model understands. It powers the Enhance button.
